title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. S is a base scheme, F a locally free O_S-module of rank 2, and G a form of GL(2)_S, PGL(2)_S. The projective line P = P(F) has sections x corresponding to lines D ⊂ F. To such a section x one attaches the unipotent radical, a sub-Module N = D°⊗D of End(F) consisting of the u with u(F) ⊂ D and u(D) = 0. This is formula (20)-(21) on the previous page.

Data. ρ and σ are sections of G (tilde denotes the image in PGL). The quotient ρ̃σ̃^{-1} = ε̃_1 is assumed unipotent; this is condition (16), with lift ε_1 = -ρσ^{-1}. Being unipotent, ε_1 = 1 + N_1 with N_1 a section of the radical 𝒩_1 attached to a section x_1 of P, corresponding to a subgroup L_1 (margin NB).

Proposition. The following are equivalent:
(i) ε_1 is regular, i.e. ≠ 1 in every fibre (equivalently N_1 is a basis of 𝒩_1), and ρ̃^{-1}(x_1) is a section of P that is fibrewise distinct from x_1.
(ii) The same with σ̃^{-1} in place of ρ̃^{-1}.
(i bis), (ii bis) The same with ρ̃, σ̃ in place of their inverses.
(iii) c = λ_0 Tr ρ + Tr σ is invertible. This is condition (42); λ_0 is a normalising scalar.

Proof.
- (i) ⇔ (ii): ρ̃σ̃^{-1} lies in the subgroup L̃_1, which normalises/fixes x_1. Hence ρ̃^{-1}(x_1) = σ̃^{-1}(x_1).
- (i) ⇔ (iii): reduce to S = Spec of an algebraically closed field and to λ_0 = 1 (replace ρ by λ_0ρ).
- If ε_1 = 1, then ρ = -σ, so c = Tr ρ + Tr σ = 0. Thus (iii) forces regularity of ε_1.
- Conversely, suppose ε_1 = 1 + N_1 is regular and ρ = -ε_1σ. Then c = Tr σ - Tr(ε_1σ) = -Tr(N_1σ). Take a basis e_0, e_1 with D = ⟨e_1⟩ and N_1 = [[0,0],[1,0]], and write σ = [[a,b],[c,d]]. Then Tr(N_1σ) = b, which is invertible iff D + σD = F, i.e. iff σ^{-1}(x_1) ≠ x_1.

Consequence (next page). Under these conditions, L_0 = ρ̃^{-1}L_1 = σ̃^{-1}L_1 and L_1 define two fibrewise-opposite Borels B_0, B_1. Their intersection T = B_0 ∩ B_1 is a maximal torus, and x_1 = ρ̃x_0 = σ̃x_0.

Purpose. This is part of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. Grothendieck is analysing pairs of elements of a form of GL(2)/PGL(2) (images of generators, as in the modular group, where the product of the order-2 and order-3 generators is unipotent) whose quotient is unipotent. The aim is to normalise them relative to a pair of opposite Borels and a torus, i.e. to put the pair in a standard 'triangular' form over an arbitrary base.
errors: On the next page, σe_1 is written as a e_0 + b e_1. With σ = [[a,b],[c,d]] acting on column vectors, actually σe_1 = b e_0 + d e_1. The conclusion (D + σD = F iff b is invertible) is unaffected.
Statement (i) mentions x_∞ while the margin and the proof use x_1. This is a notational inconsistency, which the margin NB itself flags.

ideas.what: For a regular unipotent ε = 1+N in a rank-2 form and an automorphism σ, Tr(Nσ) is invertible iff σ moves the line D = ker N = im N fibrewise. This gives a criterion for two Borels to be opposite, hence for their intersection to be a maximal torus.
ideas.modern_name: opposite Borel subgroups / transversality of points on a P^1-bundle; trace criterion
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard linear algebra / SGA3-style reductive group schemes (Demazure–Grothendieck)
ideas.where_published: Background notions of Borels, tori and forms of PGL(2) over a base are in SGA 3; this specific criterion is not known to be published.

ideas.what: Pairs (ρ, σ) in a form of GL(2) with unipotent quotient, studied over a general base scheme as a step toward normalising solutions of the 'loop equation'.
ideas.modern_name: families of PGL(2)-representations of the modular group / moduli of such representations
ideas.where_published: Possibly related themes in La Longue Marche (1981); unsure

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary, correct linear-algebra lemma over a base scheme. It is a technical step in a larger unpublished computation, with no new idea on this page by itself.
transcription_corrections: 'forme de GL(1)_S' should almost certainly read 'forme de GL(2)_S' (F is of rank 2 and traces of 2×2 matrices are used).
In (i), the image's 'x_∞' (ρ̃^{-1}(x_∞) ≠ x_∞) is meant as x_1, per the margin note 'on a désigné par x_1 la section de P sur S correspondant à L_1'.
'OPS que S est le spectre d'un corps alg clos, [?] non vide' should read roughly 'OPS que S est le spectre d'un corps alg clos, si on veut' (the reduction to geometric fibres).
